plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: Wild poinsettias are tall, leggy shrubs. Their fiery red bracts look like petals and surround tiny yellow flower clusters. The bracts are what make the plant glow against the dry-season landscape.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (roughly November to February) in its native range
plants.location: Southern Mexico, including the seasonally dry forests of Guerrero and Oaxaca
plants.funFact: The showy red parts of a poinsettia are modified leaves called bracts. The true flowers are the small yellow buds in the center. The Aztecs used the plant to make a reddish dye.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: In the southern spring, jacarandas cover city streets in lavender-blue trumpet-shaped flowers. When the blossoms fall, they leave a purple carpet beneath the trees. The feathery, fern-like foliage gives the canopy a soft look.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (about October to early December)
plants.location: Streets and parks of Pretoria, South Africa, and Sydney and Brisbane, Australia
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America, but it is now best known in Pretoria, which is nicknamed the Jacaranda City. A common saying in Australia holds that if a jacaranda flower falls on your head, you will have good luck.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: Sasanqua camellias bloom in the cold months, when most gardens are dormant. They carry delicate, often fragrant single or semi-double blooms among glossy evergreen leaves. Bees and other pollinators still active in autumn and early winter visit them.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (roughly October to December)
plants.location: Southern Japan, and gardens across the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias are close relatives of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Seeds of some camellias are pressed to make camellia oil, which has long been used in Japan for hair and skin care.
